extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, and researchers seeking a biography and career overview of Aziz Ansari
extracted.subtask_description: A biographical and career-summary page for a professional comedian/actor that documents mediums, genres, subjects, major works, awards, collaborations, touring, controversies, and creative roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the primary media in which Ansari works and publishes (e.g., stand-up specials, TV series like Parks and Recreation and Master of None, film appearances, and his book Modern Romance). Indicates the expected formats to evaluate or produce work for this performer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Observational comedy; blue comedy; sketch comedy; surreal humor; satire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the stylistic categories Ansari operates in; useful for assessing tone, audience expectations, and the appropriate conventions for material (e.g., sketch structure vs. observational set).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Indian culture; everyday life; current events; popular culture; human interaction; human sexuality; racism; self-deprecation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies recurring thematic content in Ansari's material — topics that his work commonly addresses and that inform the perspective and boundaries of his comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy style — focus on personal life / originality
rubrics_metrics.description: "Ansari's comedy style tends to focus on aspects of his personal life. 'I like talking about things that are going on in my life, because that's always going to be different and original'".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes personal-experience-driven material as a criterion for originality and distinctiveness; suggests that drawing on unique personal detail is a deliberate stylistic choice and evaluative dimension for his stand-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stand-up special distribution and release platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Specials released on Comedy Central Records, Netflix, and his own website (e.g., Intimate Moments for a Sensual Evening — Comedy Central Records, 2010; Dangerously Delicious — released on his website, 2012; several specials on Netflix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents the platforms and modes of release used for stand-up specials; useful for evaluating reach, production values, and platform-specific expectations (length, censorship, audience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Touring and live performance venues
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive touring with named tours and venues (Glow in the Dark Tour; Dangerously Delicious with stops including Bonnaroo and Carnegie Hall; Live at Madison Square Garden; performances with other headliners at Paramount Theatre).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates scale and prestige of live performances as measures of career status and the nature of live show production; venue and tour scope are evaluative markers for a comedian's success and audience size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards and nominations cited include Emmys (Outstanding Writing for a Comedy Series), Golden Globe (Best Actor – Television Series Musical or Comedy), Peabody Award, Grammy nomination for Best Comedy Album, inclusion in Time 100.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses formal awards and honors as objective metrics of critical recognition and achievement across television writing/acting and recorded comedy; specific awards tied to particular works (e.g., Master of None).

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative roles and multi-hyphenate involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Ansari is described as actor, comedian, filmmaker; he co-created, wrote, directed, and executive-produced (e.g., Master of None; also credited as director/writer/producer on Good Fortune).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats breadth of creative responsibilities (creator, writer, director, star, producer) as a criterion for evaluating artistic authorship, creative control, and professional scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborations, troupes, and creative networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Associations with Upright Citizens Brigade Theatre, Human Giant (with Rob Huebel, Paul Scheer, Jason Woliner), Food Club (with Eric Wareheim and Jason Woliner), and collaborations with other comedians (e.g., Dave Chappelle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights collaborative projects and troupe membership as dimensions of creative approach, production method (sketch vs. solo stand-up), and peer network influence on material and opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to controversy and incorporating current events into material
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the 2018 sexual-misconduct allegation and hiatus, Ansari resumed performing in 2019 with material that "was a response to the events of that past year, and touched on topics ranging from cultural appropriation, racism to sexual misconduct."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Takes account of how a comedian addresses public controversies and topical issues in subsequent work; responsiveness and framing of sensitive subjects is an evaluative dimension for tone, vulnerability, and audience reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public controversies and career impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The page documents a January 2018 accusation published on Babe.net, widespread media disagreement about whether the incident constituted sexual misconduct, critique of journalistic handling, and Ansari's brief withdrawal from the public eye followed by a return to stand-up in May 2018/2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames handling of public allegations, media narratives, and career pauses/resumptions as relevant to evaluating a public figure's reputation management, ethical scrutiny, and how controversies affect professional trajectory and audience reception.
